items.snippet: WASHINGTON, Aug 27 (Reuters) - Wall Street's most powerful banks fought side by side for years to relax capital rules, but with victory in sight, that alliance has fractured. As the Federal Reserve wraps up a sweeping overhaul of capital rules, JPMorgan, Bank of America, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are feuding over a tweak with billions of dollars at stake, according to public documents and ‌four people familiar with the matter.
items.title: Wall St banks turn on each other as capital fight nears endgame

items.snippet: Meta (NASDAQ:META) is facing renewed international scrutiny over protections for younger social media users after agreeing a settlement of up to $18 billion with nearly 50 US states, a development regulators say demonstrates that technology companies have tools available to strengthen online safeguards. The agreement, which addresses claims concerning the impact of Facebook and Instagram on teenagers, could influence how governments approach social media regulation worldwide.
